steps: Hold both hands in slightly curved B handshapes, thumbs resting alongside the palms.
Start low in front of your torso with the fingertips of both hands nearly touching at the center.
Sweep both hands upward and outward in matching arcs to outline the basket's widening sides.
Keep your palms facing inward toward each other through the whole tracing motion.
Finish with your hands apart at roughly shoulder width, glancing at the shape you outlined.
tip: Plural of “Basket” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Hold both hands flat with the fingers together and palms facing each other.
Raise both hands to the sides of your head near your ears, like blinders on a horse.
Push both hands a short distance forward and away from your head.
Keep your palms facing inward toward each other through the whole forward push.
Direct a steady gaze toward the person you are addressing to reinforce the meaning.
tip: Plural of “Attention” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Raise both hands with the index fingers extended and the other fingers folded into fists.
Start at the top-left corner of the shape in the signing space before your chest.
Trace the outline of a square: right, then down, then left, then back up.
Keep your fingertips pointing forward and your palms angled slightly toward each other.
Use a confident neutral expression, mouthing the word lightly only if it helps clarity.
tip: Plural of “Square” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Close both hands into fists with your thumbs resting against the fingers, forming A handshapes.
Hold your right fist near your chest and your left fist beside your abdomen, both a couple of inches off your body.
Thump both fists onto your body at the same time, bouncing them out and back in with a double in-out-in motion.
Keep your palms facing your body and your elbows relaxed as both hands land together.
Wear a straight, serious expression — the sign pictures a soldier gripping a rifle across the body.
tip: Plural of “Army” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Shape your dominant hand into a loose N: fold your index and middle fingers down over your tucked thumb.
Close your non-dominant hand into a fist and hold it steady in front of your chest.
Move the N hand in one clockwise circle in the air just above the fist.
Set the N hand down firmly on the back of the fist, like planting a flag.
Keep your face composed and official — this is a formal word, not a casual one.
tip: Plural of “Nation” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Bend your dominant index and middle fingers down into a tight inverted V, like two bent legs.
Hold the V hand in the neutral space in front of you, fingertips pointing down toward the ground.
Arc the hand upward and forward in a quick leaping path, then land it back at its starting height.
Let your wrist lead the motion so the two fingers ride the arc like legs springing off the ground.
Finish with a light, springy expression — this sign is for people or primates leaping, nothing else.
tip: “Jumps” is signed with the base JUMP sign.

steps: Bend your dominant index and middle fingers down into a tight inverted V, like two bent legs.
Hold the V hand in the neutral space in front of you, fingertips pointing down toward the ground.
Arc the hand upward and forward in a quick leaping path, then land it back at its starting height.
Let your wrist lead the motion so the two fingers ride the arc like legs springing off the ground.
Finish with a light, springy expression — this sign is for people or primates leaping, nothing else.
tip: “Jumping” is signed with the base JUMP sign — ASL/BSL marks ongoing action on the sign, not with a separate word.

steps: Bend your dominant index and middle fingers down into a tight inverted V, like two bent legs.
Hold the V hand in the neutral space in front of you, fingertips pointing down toward the ground.
Arc the hand upward and forward in a quick leaping path, then land it back at its starting height.
Let your wrist lead the motion so the two fingers ride the arc like legs springing off the ground.
Finish with a light, springy expression — this sign is for people or primates leaping, nothing else.
tip: Past form of “Jump” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Shape both hands into clawed 5s, fingers spread and lightly curved.
Bring the two hands together at chest height in front of you.
Touch the fingertips of the hands together lightly, twice in a row.
Aim the palms inward toward each other as the hands meet.
Keep a neutral face, widening your eyes slightly for a bigger ball.
tip: Plural of “Ball” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Extend the index and middle fingers on both hands.
Hold the hands side by side at chest height, fingertips toward each other.
Wiggle the dominant fingers toward the other hand's fingertips in small pulses.
Angle the palms inward so the fingertips nearly meet.
Use a neutral or warm expression suited to describing a pair of people.
tip: Plural of “Couple” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand flat and steady, fingers pressed together.
Keep it in front of your torso at waist height.
Walk your dominant fingertips along its back until they slip off the end.
Point the dominant fingertips forward as they travel and drop off.
Match your face to the outcome — sad for a bad ending, bright for a good one.
tip: Plural of “Ending” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Raise your dominant hand with the index finger extended and the other fingers folded into a loose fist.
Hold your non-dominant hand open and flat at chest height with its palm facing upward.
Tap the side of your dominant index finger down onto the open palm of your non-dominant hand.
Repeat the tapping motion at least once more, keeping the movement quick and crisp.
Keep your dominant palm facing sideways as the index finger strikes the opposite palm.
Use a neutral, engaged expression, as if raising points in a back-and-forth debate.
tip: “Discusses” is signed with the base DISCUSS sign.

steps: Raise your dominant hand with the index finger extended and the other fingers folded into a loose fist.
Hold your non-dominant hand open and flat at chest height with its palm facing upward.
Tap the side of your dominant index finger down onto the open palm of your non-dominant hand.
Repeat the tapping motion at least once more, keeping the movement quick and crisp.
Keep your dominant palm facing sideways as the index finger strikes the opposite palm.

tip: “Discussing” is signed with the base DISCUSS sign — ASL/BSL marks ongoing action on the sign, not with a separate word.

steps: Raise your dominant hand with the index finger extended and the other fingers folded into a loose fist.
Hold your non-dominant hand open and flat at chest height with its palm facing upward.
Tap the side of your dominant index finger down onto the open palm of your non-dominant hand.

steps: Hold both hands loosely open in front of your torso, fingers relaxed and slightly apart.
Keep both palms angled toward each other as you begin pulling your hands inward.
Draw both hands back toward your chest in one smooth, welcoming motion.
Close your fingers into flat O shapes as your hands arrive at your chest, as if gathering something in.
End with your fingertips near your upper chest and your palms facing your body.
Pair the motion with an open, willing expression — you are taking the offer in.
tip: “Accepts” is signed with the base ACCEPT sign.

steps: Hold both hands loosely open in front of your torso, fingers relaxed and slightly apart.

steps: Extend the index finger of your non-dominant hand and hold it upright at about eye level.
Extend the index finger of your dominant hand and aim it toward the tip of the base finger.
Move your dominant hand forward toward the base finger in a deliberate, aiming motion.
Stop just short of contact, hovering close to the fingertip like an arrow nearing a target.
Keep both palms angled inward so the two fingertips line up with each other.
Hold a focused, intent expression — you are locking onto a target, not touching it.
tip: Plural of “Goal” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Extend the index finger of your dominant hand, curling the rest of the fingers into a fist.
Hold your non-dominant hand flat and horizontal with the palm facing down.
Push your dominant index finger straight up between the fingers of the flat base hand.
Make the pop-up quick and sudden, as if the finger is surprising everyone by surfacing.
Keep your dominant palm facing sideways while the finger shoots upward through the base hand.
Raise your eyebrows with a slightly startled look — something has just turned up.
tip: “Appears” is signed with the base APPEAR sign.

steps: Curl both hands into E handshapes, folding the fingertips down to meet the thumbs.
Hold both fists up in front of your shoulders, a few inches apart.
Shake both hands frantically from side to side in short, rapid bursts.
Keep the shaking tight and urgent, like an alarm that will not stop ringing.
Turn your palms to face each other as the hands rattle back and forth.
Wear a wide-eyed, alarmed expression — your face must match the urgency of the hands.
tip: Plural of “Emergency” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Pinch the thumb and index finger of each hand together to form two F handshapes.
Hold both F hands in front of your lower chest with the fingers pointing slightly down.
Drive both hands downward in one short, firm stroke, as if stamping a decision.
Stop the hands abruptly at the end of the stroke — the sudden halt carries the finality.
Keep your palms angled toward each other while the F hands drop together.
Set your jaw with a firm, resolved expression — the matter is settled.
tip: “Determines” is signed with the base DETERMINE sign.

steps: Pinch the thumb and index finger of each hand together to form two F handshapes.

Stop the hands abruptly at the end of the stroke — the sudden halt carries the finality.

steps: Point the index finger of your dominant hand straight ahead with the palm facing down.
Raise the index finger of your non-dominant hand upright in front of your chest.
Slide the side of your dominant index finger up and down along the side of the raised finger.
Repeat the sliding motion several times with short, quick strokes, like mercury in a thermometer.
Keep your dominant palm facing down throughout, which keeps it distinct from the MONTH sign.
Hold a neutral, inquiring expression, as if asking about the reading on a gauge.
tip: Plural of “Temperature” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Bring both hands up and touch your fingertips together to form a small peaked rooftop.
Hold the rooftop peak in the signing space in front of your face or upper chest.
Trace a small, quick circle in the air with the rooftop shape, like a ring of little huts.
Keep your palms angled downward and facing each other while the rooftop travels in its circle.
Use a warm storytelling expression — this storybook version suits children's tales, not everyday chat.
tip: Plural of “Village” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Form your dominant hand into a G handshape, with thumb and index finger pinched together.
Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of you, palm facing upward, as a steady base.
Tumble the G hand forward in a full somersault movement above the base hand.
Land the pinched G hand down onto the open palm of the base hand.
Keep your expression neutral; this describes an accomplishment, not a question.
tip: “Graduating” is signed with the base GRADUATE sign — ASL/BSL marks ongoing action on the sign, not with a separate word.

steps: Form your dominant hand into a G handshape, with thumb and index finger pinched together.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand out flat in front of you with its palm facing down.
Raise your dominant hand and extend only the index and middle fingers together.
Rest the two extended fingers on top of the flat hand, as if sitting on it.
Tap the fingers down twice with small firm taps — this is the noun CHAIR.
Point the fingertips straight down onto the hand, keeping the palm angled downward.
Keep your face neutral; a single tap instead of two changes it to the verb SIT.
tip: Plural of “Chair” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Form the letter B with your dominant hand, holding it at chest height.
Flick smoothly through the letters U and S in one quick blended motion.
Let the handshapes blur together instead of pausing on each separate letter.
Keep the movement compact in neutral signing space in front of your torso.
Angle your palm forward or slightly sideways for a comfortable clear read.
Maintain a neutral expression; mouthing the word lightly can help in low context.
tip: Plural of “Bus” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Open both hands into loose 5 handshapes with all fingers spread wide apart.
Hold your non-dominant hand palm-up at waist height as a flat base.
Lay the back of your dominant palm-up hand onto the other open palm.
Swipe the dominant hand outward and off the base hand in one careless flick.
Keep the dominant palm facing upward through the swipe, as if tossing something away.
Wear a slightly dismissive expression — the sign carries a careless who-cares attitude.
tip: “Wastes” is signed with the base WASTE sign.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of you, palm facing up like a page.
Form the letter D with your dominant hand, keeping the fingers rounded and upright.
Place the D hand on the flat palm and slide it forward, like flipping a page.
Repeat the slide a second time with a small crisp motion to finish the sign.
Angle the D palm slightly inward toward your body as your hand glides forward.
Keep your expression neutral and focused, like someone scanning a wordbook for a definition.
tip: Plural of “Dictionary” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Close both fists as if gripping a fishing rod, your dominant hand above the other.
Hold the rod out in front of your body at waist level.
Swing the rod up and forward in a casting motion, then repeat the cast a second time.
Keep your palms facing down toward the ground through the whole cast.
Keep your face neutral and your eyes toward the imagined line landing spot.
tip: “Fishings” is signed with the base FISHING sign.

steps: Curl the fingers of both hands at the middle knuckles into loose claw handshapes.
Hold your hands out in front of your chest with the fingertips nearly touching.
Interlock the clawed fingers of the two hands like gears meshing together in a machine.
Raise and lower the locked hands twice together, mimicking moving gears.
Keep the backs of your hands angled toward the sides through the motion.
Keep your expression neutral; a slight lean forward adds mechanical emphasis.
tip: Plural of “Motor” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Shape both hands into loose flattened O handshapes, fingertips and thumbs nearly touching.
Hold both hands up near your temples, in front of your head.
Push both hands forward about six inches in one quick motion, as if passing knowledge onward.
Open both hands into flat B handshapes with the palms facing each other.
Lower the flat hands straight down in front of your body to mark the person.
Keep a calm, respectful expression; a slight nod suits the formal title.
tip: Plural of “Professor” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Shape your dominant hand into a flattened O, thumb pad pressed under the fingertips.
Hold your non-dominant hand low in front of you, fingers together and palm cupped upward as the base.
Move the dominant hand down and settle it into the base hand, as if placing an object where it belongs.
Keep the dominant fingertips pointing down as they land, with the base palm staying open and level.
Keep your face and shoulders neutral; this is a plain placing gesture, not an emphatic one.
tip: “Installs” is signed with the base INSTALL sign.

steps: Pinch the thumb against the index finger on each hand, forming two small pincers.
Grip your shirt fabric on each side of your upper chest, pinching between thumb and index finger.
Tug the fabric outward away from your body two or three times in short, even pulls.
Keep your palms angled down and slightly inward while you pinch and tug.
Use a neutral, describing expression — you are naming the garment, not offering to help.
tip: Plural of “Shirt” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Shape your dominant hand into an F, thumb touching the index fingertip to close the circle.
Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of you at chest height, palm facing straight up.
Touch the pinched tip of the F hand to the base palm near its heel, then slide it forward twice.
Keep the base palm level and facing up; turn the F hand's palm sideways during the slides.
Count with a focused, neutral face — this is a tallying motion, not a question.
tip: “Counts” is signed with the base COUNT sign.

steps: Bring up your dominant hand with the fingers held together and straight.
Start with the fingertips touching the center of your left breast.
Lift slightly and bring the fingertips down onto the center of your right breast in an even second touch.
Keep your palm turned toward your body so the fingertips land flat on the chest.
Keep your face matter-of-fact — BREAST is an anatomical term, not an emotional one.
tip: Plural of “Breast” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Shape both hands into bent hands with your fingers curled at the knuckles, palms facing down.

steps: Make a fist with your non-dominant hand and hold it upright in front of your chest.

Rest the tip of your dominant middle finger on top of the upright fist.
Circle your dominant hand around the fingertip, palm angled downward, as if the earth spins on its axis.

steps: Point both index fingers forward.
Move both hands forward together.

steps: Bring your bunched fingertips to your mouth.
Repeat once or twice, as if putting food in your mouth.

Reach the open hand out toward the person or object you are taking from.

Turn your palm to face yourself as the fist arrives at your chest.

tip: Past form of “Take” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Touch the fingertips of your flat hand to the side of your forehead.
Move them slightly outward.

steps: Touch your dominant thumb to your fingertips to make a flattened O handshape.
Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of you, palm facing up.
Set the flattened O onto the open palm, then slide it forward and off the hand.
Keep the moving hand's palm angled down as it brushes along and leaves the base palm.

steps: Point your dominant index finger forward, other fingers tucked away.
Start with the fingertip resting near your chin.
Move the hand forward in a short arc, as if flipping a word off your chin.
Aim the motion at the person being told; pull toward yourself for TELL-ME.

tip: Past form of “Tell” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of you, palm up, as your paper.

Scribble a quick side-to-side motion across the palm.

tip: Past form of “Write” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Close both hands into S fists, thumbs across the fingers, like gripping a steering wheel.

Move both hands in alternating forward-and-back motions, as if steering.

Make the motion larger and directional for DRIVE; a small repeated bounce means the noun CAR.
tip: Past form of “Drive” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Pinch your dominant index fingertip against your thumb, like picking something up.

Keep your palm facing down as you pull the choice in.
Nod slightly as you finish — choosing is a decisive act.
tip: Past form of “Choose” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Form a C with your hand as if holding a cup.

tip: Past form of “Drink” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Make L handshapes with both hands, extending the index finger and thumb.
Hook your dominant thumb around your non-dominant index finger to link the hands.
Wiggle both index fingers alternately while pushing both hands forward together.
Keep both palms facing down so the wiggling fingers read as legs.
Move with energy and lean slightly forward, as if you are really sprinting.
tip: Past form of “Run” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand out flat, spreading only the index and middle fingers.
Place your dominant index finger at the base of those two spread fingers.
Twist the dominant index finger once, as if turning a small key.

Wear an alert, ready expression that matches a fresh beginning.
tip: Past form of “Begin” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand in an S fist, steady in front of your body.

Sweep the dominant hand inward toward your body, closing it into an S fist as it goes.
Lift the closed fist upward, finishing above your non-dominant hand.
Finish with a proud, triumphant expression.
tip: Past form of “Win” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Touch the tip of your dominant thumb to the tip of your index finger, making a flattened O.
Hold the hand at chest level, a few inches in front of your torso.
Make a quick small lifting motion, as if you are picking up the thing you just spotted.
Keep your palm facing down through the whole quick movement.
Brighten your face with a look of discovery, like your search just ended.
tip: Past form of “Find” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Bend your dominant index finger into a slight hook, like a small tapping finger.
Tap the side of your ear twice with the tip of your hooked index finger.
Keep your palm facing outward and your elbow relaxed at your side while you tap.
Use a light, quick double-tap right at the ear opening for a clean production.
Keep your face neutral and your eyes on your conversation partner.
tip: Past form of “Hear” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Shape both hands into K handshapes, with the middle finger resting on the thumb and the index and pinky fingers extended.
Hold your non-dominant K hand out to the side of your body, steady and still as the base.
Swing your dominant K hand in one quick downward motion onto the non-dominant K hand.
Let the pinky-side edge of the dominant hand land firmly on the top of the base hand.
Keep the base hand frozen through the whole movement; only the dominant hand travels.
Pair the sign with a firm, decisive expression when signing it as a command like keep it.
tip: Past form of “Keep” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Extend both index fingers upright, keeping your other fingers and thumbs tucked closed.
Hold the hands out in front of your chest about a foot apart, with your palms facing each other.
Bring the two hands toward each other until their lower edges meet in the middle.
Do not let the fingertips touch — the meeting happens at the base of the hands.
Aim the movement between the two people or spots to show who is meeting whom.
Keep your eyes on the meeting point and give a slight nod for a friendly greeting.
tip: Past form of “Meet” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of you with the palm facing up.
Touch the tip of your dominant index finger to the center of the open palm.
Flick the index finger forward off the palm toward the person being paid.
Keep the moving finger's palm facing sideways during the flick.
Aim the flick at the recipient and keep your expression matter-of-fact.
tip: Past form of “Pay” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Point the index and middle fingers of your dominant hand straight down in a V, like legs.
Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of you, palm facing up, as the ground.
Set the V fingertips down onto the palm and hold them still, standing upright.
Keep the V fingers pointing straight down, palm facing sideways.
Hold a tall, upright posture yourself — your body mirrors the sign.
tip: Past form of “Stand” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Hold your index finger up beside your temple.
Flick it upward sharply.
tip: Past form of “Understand” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Shape both hands into bent hands with your fingers curled at the knuckles, palms facing down.
Hold your hands in front of your chest in neutral signing space.
Lay one bent hand across the top of the other hand.
Lift the lower hand over and stack it on top, moving upward with each layer.
Alternate the hands several times, each stack rising higher, as if building a brick wall.
tip: Past form of “Build” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Touch your dominant thumb to your fingertips to make a flattened O handshape.
Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of you, palm facing up.
Set the flattened O onto the open palm, then slide it forward and off the hand.
Keep the moving hand's palm angled down as it brushes along and leaves the base palm.
Face the direction of the seller, since the forward motion shows money changing hands.
tip: “Buying” is signed with the base BUY sign — ASL/BSL marks ongoing action on the sign, not with a separate word.

steps: Shape both hands into flat open hands with fingertips together, like the starting position of the PLEASE sign.
Place your right flat hand on your upper chest and your left flat hand on your belly, an inch or two out from your body.
Circle both hands at the same time in opposite directions, with the right hand looping clockwise and the left hand counterclockwise.
Angle your palms inward toward your torso so the fingertips of each hand point toward the other hand.
Wear a warm, content smile while signing, since the sign conveys pleasure and delight.
tip: Past form of “Enjoy” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Make Y handshapes with both hands, thumbs and pinkies extended.
Hold both Y-hands in front of your chest, a few inches apart.
Twist both wrists back and forth in a playful alternating shake.
Keep the palms facing toward each other through the whole shake.
Smile and look lively, since PLAY always carries a fun feeling.

steps: Form a Y-handshape with your dominant hand by stretching your thumb and pinkie wide while folding the middle fingers down.
Raise the hand to chest height in front of you with the palm facing down.
Press the hand firmly downward in one short, decisive stroke, as if pinning something in place.
Hold the Y-handshape rigid the whole time, keeping the thumb and pinkie fully extended.
Repeat the downward press with both hands together when you want extra emphasis.
Keep a firm, settled expression — this is a command to hold position, not a question.
tip: Past form of “Stay” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.
